key_insight: Increasing polymer relaxation time drives settling spheres in a polymer solution from regular sedimentation into a chaotic, intermittent elastic pseudoturbulence with clustering and enhanced large-scale motion.
engineering_relevance: Viscoelasticity can strongly alter sedimentation rates and flow stability in particle-laden processes, so polymer choice and relaxation time are critical design variables in suspensions, separations, and slurry transport.
method: Particle-resolved direct numerical simulations of settling spheres in a viscoelastic fluid
Low density ratio and low Galilei number sedimentation regime examined across increasing Deborah number
Analysis of clustering, velocity spectra, and high-order velocity structure functions
evidence_signal: The abstract reports gravity-aligned clusters, faster settling, a -4 high-wavenumber spectral scaling, and nonlinear high-order structure-function exponents as signatures of elastic turbulence.
watch_item: The findings are for low-Galilei, low-density-ratio conditions, so the same behavior may not directly transfer to denser, more inertial, or higher-concentration suspensions.
paper_title: Elastic pseudoturbulence induced by low-Galilei settling spheres
